newsitem.title: USA: Clinton sends Yeltsin letter on NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sends Yeltsin letter on NATO expansion.

text.p: President Bill Clinton sent Russian President Boris Yeltsin a long letter discussing the expansion of NATO and other European security questions, the White House said on Friday.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Secretary of State Madeleine Albright handed the letter to Yeltsin when she met him in the Kremlin earlier on Friday.

"Most of the substance of the president's letter dealt with issues related to European security, specifically the future of Europe, the future of NATO and the obvious question of NATO's expansion and Russia's relationship to NATO as we move forward," said McCurry.
"There's a lot of hard work left on that subject," he said. "Part of that hard work is reflected in the correspondence the president exchanged with President Yeltsin."
McCurry said Clinton also added a personal note saying he was glad to see Yeltsin up and at work after recent illnesses.
Albright said in Moscow the United States and Russia had made progress on a European security deal, but there had been no breakthrough after two days of intensive talks.
She said it was far from certain that a deal could be in place by the July NATO summit in Madrid that will decide which former Soviet-bloc states to bring in as new members of the western alliance.
Russia vehemently opposes the eastward expansion of NATO which would take the organisation to the borders of the former Soviet Union.
Moscow has already warned NATO that its plans to grant membership to some of Moscow's Cold War allies in central and eastern Europe could upset the European security balance.
